slides.label: Integration
slides.notes: Open by turning integration into a measurement story. Previous chapters built forms as pointwise meters for directed inputs. Chapter 37 asks what happens when those local readings are sampled over a directed geometric object and added. Emphasize the route: orient the domain, pull the form back to parameters, sum small contributions, and watch interior boundary terms cancel into Stokes theorem.

slides.label: What Does A Form Integral Add?
slides.notes: Slow down the input data before formulas appear. A k-form cannot be integrated over an arbitrary object; it needs an oriented k-dimensional domain, or a chain made from such pieces. The diagram separates the curve, surface patch, and volume cell cases. The common operation is the same: evaluate the form on oriented tangent directions and add scalar readings.

slides.label: Line Integrals Pull A 1-Form To Time
slides.notes: Use the path picture to make pullback concrete. A curve gamma converts a one-form on the ambient space into an ordinary density on the interval of time. The vector gamma prime supplies the directed input at each sample. Reparameterizing the same oriented curve changes the speed and the time step together, so the integral remains a geometric reading.

slides.label: Exact Forms Collapse To Endpoints
slides.notes: Make exactness operational, not merely symbolic. If omega is df, each small line-integral contribution is an infinitesimal change in the potential f. Summing along the path telescopes, so only the endpoint values remain. This explains path independence, zero loop integrals for exact forms, and why potential level pictures are the right visual test.

slides.label: Pullback Is The Coordinate Contract
slides.notes: This slide names the bookkeeping that makes integration coordinate-ready. A parameterization phi lets the instructor compute on a simple domain while measuring the original geometry. The pullback phi star omega feeds parameter tangent vectors through d phi before omega evaluates them. Orientation is part of the contract: reversing the parameter orientation flips the integral sign.

slides.label: Partitions Make Boundary Terms Cancel
slides.notes: Present Stokes first as local cancellation. Break a region into oriented cells and apply the boundary measurement to each cell. Every shared interior edge is traversed twice with opposite orientations, so those contributions cancel. Only the outer boundary remains. The exterior derivative is the interior density whose small-cell integral records this boundary accumulation.

slides.label: Generalized Stokes Is The Accounting Identity
slides.notes: Now state the theorem as the compact form of the cancellation story. The left side integrates the derivative over the oriented manifold, while the right side integrates the original form over the induced boundary orientation. The bar chart from the notebook is used as an accounting reminder: signs and boundary conventions are structural data, not decoration.

slides.label: Classical Theorems Are Shadows
slides.notes: Use this as a unification slide rather than a formula dump. Green, vector-calculus Stokes, the divergence theorem, and Cauchy's theorem differ in the degree of the form and the geometric domain. Once the relevant form is chosen, each says the same thing: an interior derivative measurement equals the accumulated boundary measurement.

slides.label: Closed Need Not Mean Exact
slides.notes: Introduce the topological catch. A closed form has zero exterior derivative, so locally it looks like it should be a derivative of a potential. On a punctured domain, loops can wind around missing geometry. The vortex period detects that obstruction: the local derivative vanishes, but a global loop integral can remain nonzero.

slides.label: Integration Diagnostics
slides.notes: Close with habits students can reuse. Before integrating a form, ask which oriented domain is being measured, what parameterization supplies the pullback, which partitions are allowed to cancel, and whether topology leaves a period behind. The five notebook artifacts become a compact review path from local measurement to Stokes and then to de Rham cohomology.
